newsitem.title: USA: Disaster reserve plan 'not going anywhere'--USDA.
newsitem.headline: Disaster reserve plan 'not going anywhere'--USDA.

text.p: Congressional opposition means a proposal to use U.S. export funds to replenish disaster stockpiles "is not going anywhere," a high-ranking Agriculture Department official said Wednesday.
"Without legislative authority, it isn't going anywhere," said Gus Schumacher, head of the Foreign Agriculture Service.
Senator Pat Roberts, Kansas Republican, said that based on his conversations with Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, "the secretary will not push this any further."

USDA officials floated the idea last week of using unneeded export promotion funds to rebuild the four-million-tonne Food Security Commodity Reserve. Farm-state lawmakers were quick to criticize the idea as harmful to U.S. exports.
No effort has been made to put the idea into legislation.

Senator Tom Harkin, Iowa Democrat, said wheat-state farmers misrepresented the likely impact of the idea. The reserve is tiny compared to U.S. grain output, Harkin said, after noting his state's major crop -- corn -- has never been subsidized for export.
"There are some of us up here who are going to fight for disaster reserves," Harkin said.
